clue.text: Engineer in a car plant

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is set to work as an engineer inside a car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a job title and 'car plant' as a factory, but 'plant' is the definition and 'Engineer' tells you to rearrange IN A CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a yellow-flowered herb of the daisy family, used in bruise remedies.

clue.text: Familiar ground following cut in postal service

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
cut means the letter for following is removed

explanation.surface: A known area after a reduction in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as land but is the past tense of grind; F is removed ('cut') from FAMILIAR, leaving AMILIAR, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is the delivery of letters by aircraft, a postal service.

clue.text: Cockney hurried, initially revealing name and rank

indicators.note: initially revealing puts the abbreviation for name at the front
a Cockney speaker drops the H from the start of words

parts.note: hurried means hasty

explanation.surface: A Londoner in a rush reveals his name and military grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' seems a military grade next to 'name' but means foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means foul or offensive, as of a smell.

clue.text: Church leader in Ireland not in favour of red

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of Ireland

parts.note: anti means opposed

explanation.surface: An Irish church leader opposes communists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a political colour but is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Setback after spring floods

annotationWithheld.why: Setback after spring floods (6): the parse is SPA + SET reversed, but the single printed word 'Setback' must be both the fodder SET and the reversal indicator 'back', one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Do without current correspondence

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the party goes round

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Managing without electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity means equality, a correspondence between two things.

clue.text: Actor takes time reading a play

indicators.note: play means the letters move about freely and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer spends a while reading a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the script being read, but it rearranges READING A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Cat basket finally grabbed by cardinals

indicators.note: grabbed by means the letter goes inside the cardinals

parts.note: sevens are cardinal numbers

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of basket

explanation.surface: A cat's basket is seized by senior churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen, but means numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat Stevens is the singer-songwriter now known as Yusuf Islam.

clue.text: Jellied eels for starters — seafood devoured by male model

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letters of Jellied and eels
devoured by means the seafood is swallowed inside the man's name

parts.note: Anton is a man's name
a shrimp is seafood

explanation.surface: A male model eats Cockney eels as a first course and then shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a traditional London East End dish; 'model' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Shrimpton was a leading English fashion model of the 1960s.

clue.text: Bugs running risk

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of the next word are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Insects or computer faults taking their chances.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, the same sense as to irritate or vex.

clue.text: Reserve disappearing with this vessel?

definitions.meaning: something said or done to dispel social stiffness and coolness between strangers
a ship built to cut a channel through frozen sea

explanation.surface: A ship whose crew lose their shyness on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve here is social coolness, the frosty manner between strangers; a remark that ends it shares its name with the ship that smashes frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a conversation opener that thaws formality and a ship that clears frozen water.

clue.text: Outlaw hugging a Big Apple tree

indicators.note: hugging means the first piece wraps round the following ones

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban
the Big Apple is New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: A fugitive criminal clings to a large apple tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun, a bandit, but works as the verb meaning to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: The banyan is an Indian fig whose aerial roots grow into extra trunks.

clue.text: Toad, ignoring Jack and Edward, chewed the fat

indicators.note: ignoring means the named part is left out of the toad's name

parts.note: the natterjack is a European toad with a loud call
the word jack, removed from the end of the toad's name
Ed is the usual short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A toad pays no attention to two men named Jack and Edward and just gossips.
explanation.walkthrough: The natterjack is a British toad; dropping its 'jack' leaves NATTER, then ED is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew the fat is an idiom for chatting idly at length, like gossiping.

clue.text: Fighter pilot with boat crew

parts.note: to pilot an aircraft is to fly it
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot is joined by a rowing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter pilot' reads as an RAF airman, but 'Fighter' is the boxer being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in the lightest standard weight class.

clue.text: Come to play cricket for Yorkshire city

parts.note: to come to is to wake
to field is to play cricket as the side not batting

explanation.surface: Regaining consciousness to play a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakefield is a city in West Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Accommodation like leisure centre

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the seven-letter word leisure

explanation.surface: Lodging that resembles a sports and fitness centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' reads as a comparison but is the slang verb 'to dig'.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is informal British for rented lodgings, a room let to a lodger.

clue.text: Drink that's put in the oven?

definitions.meaning: a brand of cola soft drink
the solid fuel made by heating coal, fed to a furnace or oven

explanation.surface: A beverage that someone thinks of baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is both the cola drink and the carbon fuel burned in furnaces and stoves.

clue.text: Break a saucer? Dash it!

indicators.note: dash means smash, so the letters of a saucer are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a saucer and swears in annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash it!' reads as a mild oath but tells you to rearrange A SAUCER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesura is a pause in a line of verse.

clue.text: Happy state suggests one with half of Guinness

parts.note: to suggest is to give tips
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of takes the latter four letters of the eight-letter stout name

explanation.surface: A cheerful mood is recommended by someone drinking half a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness is an Irish stout; half of it here is its last four letters, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsiness is the mild merriment of slight drunkenness, a happy state indeed.

clue.text: Not affected as engineers

parts.note: as can mean since, giving a reason
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Unaffected in the way of engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere is genuine, without affectation.

clue.text: Animal in revolutionary American prison

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the turned letters
revolutionary means turned round

parts.note: a panda is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature is put in a rebel American jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' sounds like an American rebel but turns US round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau was a Berlin prison housing Nazi war criminals.

clue.text: It supports lots of lines in port

indicators.note: supports means in a down entry the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: odes are poems, many lines
it is sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A support for many lines in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a crossword convention for sex appeal, SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Worker not happy with reinforcement

parts.note: a worker bee
fed up means discontented

explanation.surface: An employee is dissatisfied with extra help sent in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the crossword's usual bee, the worker caste of a hive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beefed up has been strengthened, made sturdier by added support.

clue.text: A lack of publicity about illness? That's OK

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the illness

parts.note: a lack of something is no such thing
an ad is publicity
TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: Asks whether no media coverage of a disease is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not bad is mild approval, meaning acceptable or fine.

clue.text: Private plaything entertaining same-sex couple?

indicators.note: entertaining means the toy holds the pair within

parts.note: a toy is a plaything
MM is two men, M for male

explanation.surface: A toy which plays host to two people of the same sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective but is a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tommy is a British private soldier, from Tommy Atkins.

clue.text: Order to reps in certain retail outlet

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for certain

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of to reps are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A sales instruction to representatives at a particular shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command given to sales reps, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstore is a very large retail shop, often out of town.

clue.text: A bit of humidity in the south of France

indicators.note: a bit of means only a fragment inside the word is taken

explanation.surface: A touch of dampness in the air of Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Midi is the French name for the southern region of France.

clue.text: An ecclesiastic high-up like a llama?

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A lofty churchman compared to a woolly South American animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-up' seems to describe the churchman but belongs to the definition: llamas live high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas come from the Andes, so a high-dwelling llama is of those mountains.

clue.text: Copper reported parting words

indicators.note: reported means the letters are heard as spoken

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer passes on a farewell message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, whose symbol CU said letter by letter is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an everyday farewell, said when two people go separate ways.
